title: Jessalyn Sebastian
text:
I am a PhD candidate studying Statistics at UCI, advised by Dr. Volodymyr Minin. My research focuses on developing Bayesian methods that are flexible enough to address complex scientific questions but transparent and robust enough for use by practitioners. I am particularly interested in stochastic processes, latent function inference, and the role of modeling assumptions and prior choices in statistical inference, with applications in infectious disease epidemiology. I am also interested in statistics education.
My current methodological work develops computationally efficient Bayesian methods for smoothing and latent function inference using Gaussian process priors with Markov structure. I also work on collaborative applied projects using Bayesian phylogenetic methods to study respiratory virus and tuberculosis transmission.
I also spend time not doing statistics, because variety is the spice of life. I enjoy reading, writing, crochet and other handcrafts, television of many different genres, learning about medicine and human anatomy, and making coffee and tea.

title: Research
text: My research focuses on Bayesian methods for latent function inference and stochastic processes, with applications in infectious disease epidemiology. I am especially interested in computationally efficient methods and in how modeling assumptions affect statistical conclusions.

title: Teaching
text:
I approach teaching with the belief that rigor and compassion are not competing goals. My teaching is organized around four broad principles: (1) I use rigorous assessment but pair it with clear expectations; (2) I situate statistical problems in socially meaningful or scientifically relevant contexts that show students what statistics is for; (3) I engage students in authentic statistical thinking, including the choices and ambiguity that characterize statistical practice; and (4) I try to create a nonjudgmental environment where students feel able to work through uncertainty and take intellectual risks.

title: Teaching
text:
Evidence of Teaching Effectiveness
In STATS 8, 175 of 211 students (83%) completed the official end-of-term evaluation:

95% agreed or strongly agreed that material was presented in a way that helped them understand it.
93% agreed or strongly agreed that opportunities for learning helped them better understand the material.
90% agreed or strongly agreed that they would recommend me as an instructor.
85% agreed or strongly agreed that the course broadened their perspectives.

In STATS 67, students rated me 8.94/9 for accessibility and responsiveness, 8.78/9 for creating an open and fair learning environment, and 8.56/9 for encouraging students to think.

“I remember Jessalyn at the start of the quarter saying she hopes we see the world differently after this class. I have good news for her, I do.”

My full teaching portfolio includes representative course materials, annotated assessments and activities, additional student feedback, discussion of my engagement with statistics and mathematics education scholarship, and reflections on how my teaching has developed over time.
